examples.en: Public officials must be honest.
My father worked as a public servant for a long time.
The assets of public officials were disclosed.
The newly appointed official gave a greeting.
Public officials may not accept gifts.
I study to become a public official.

explain: 나라나 지방 정부 일을 하는 사람을 두루 가리켜요. 일상에서는 '공무원'이라고 더 많이 말하고, '공직자'는 뉴스나 법에서 윤리나 책임을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It covers anyone doing work for the national or local government. Everyday speech prefers 공무원, while 공직자 appears in the news and in law when talking about ethics and responsibility.

examples.en: Teachers demanded protection of their authority.

examples.ko: 교권 침해 문제가 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Violations of teachers' rights often appear in the news.

examples.ko: 학생 인권과 교권이 모두 존중돼야 해요.
examples.en: Both students' rights and teachers' rights must be respected.
These days many people say teachers' authority has collapsed.
The school discussed ways to protect teachers' rights.

examples.ko: 교권 보호를 위한 법이 새로 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: The law for protecting teachers' rights was newly revised.

explain: 학생의 권리를 말하는 '학생 인권'과 짝처럼 나오는 말로, 교사가 가르치는 일에서 존중받고 보호받을 권리를 뜻하는 쪽으로 많이 써요. '교권 침해', '교권 보호', '교권 추락'처럼 뉴스에서 자주 만나요.
explain_en: It often pairs with '학생 인권' (students' rights) and mostly refers to a teacher's right to be respected and protected in their work. You often meet it in the news as '교권 침해' (violation), '교권 보호' (protection) and '교권 추락' (decline).

examples.en: The company has as many as three business sites.

examples.ko: 이 사업장에서는 직원 오십 명이 일해요.
examples.en: Fifty employees work at this site.

examples.ko: 사업장 주소를 서류에 정확히 써 주세요.
examples.en: Please write the workplace address on the form accurately.

examples.ko: 새 사업장을 열려고 대출을 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking into a loan to open a new business site.
Safety rules differ a little at each site.

examples.ko: 외국인 근로자가 사업장을 바꾸려면 서류를 내야 해요.
examples.en: A foreign worker must submit documents to change workplaces.

explain: 서류나 법에 나오는 말로, 일하는 곳 하나하나를 가리켜요. 대화에서는 보통 '회사', '가게', '공장'이라고 하고, 사업장은 신고나 계약처럼 공식적인 자리에서 더 많이 들려요. '사업장 주소', '사업장을 옮기다'가 대표적이에요.
explain_en: This is a word from paperwork and law, pointing to each individual place where work is done. In conversation people say 회사, 가게, or 공장, while 사업장 is heard more in official settings such as filings and contracts. Typical uses are 사업장 주소 and 사업장을 옮기다.

examples.en: A training program for people who lost their jobs is opening.
I went to apply for the support fund for the unemployed.
The factory closed, so the number of jobless people grew.
My uncle was out of work for a while.

examples.ko: 실직자는 구직 상담을 무료로 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Jobless people can get job-search counseling for free.
The news said the number of people who lost their jobs has dropped.

explain: 일하던 곳에서 일자리를 잃은 사람을 가리켜요. '실업자'는 일이 없는 사람 전체를 넓게 말하지만, '실직자'는 직장을 잃었다는 점이 더 강해요. 직접 사람에게 쓰면 기분이 상할 수 있어서 뉴스나 지원 제도에서 주로 써요.
explain_en: It refers to someone who has lost the job they had. '실업자' broadly means anyone without work, while '실직자' stresses losing a job. Saying it directly to a person can hurt feelings, so it is mainly used in news and support programs.

en: being excused; exemption (from a group activity)

examples.en: Anyone who is injured is excused from today's training.

examples.ko: 저는 감기 때문에 체육 시간에 열외가 됐어요.
examples.en: Because of a cold, I was excused from P.E. class.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에서 그 사람만 열외로 두기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to leave only that person out of our team.
Nobody is excused from the cleaning this time.

examples.ko: 열외 없이 모두 회의에 참석해야 해요.
examples.en: Everyone must attend the meeting, with no exceptions.

examples.ko: 단체 사진에서 나만 열외인 것 같아 속상했어요.
examples.en: I felt upset, as if I were the only one left out of the group photo.

explain: '예외'와 비슷하지만 열외는 훈련, 청소, 모임 같은 단체 활동에서 빠지는 사람에게 써요. '열외 없이'로 모두 참여해야 한다고 말하는 경우가 많아요. 군대에서 많이 쓰는 말이라 조금 딱딱하게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is close to '예외' (exception), but 열외 is for someone excused from group activities such as training, cleaning or meetings. People often say '열외 없이' to mean everyone takes part. It is widely used in the military, so it can sound a bit stiff.

examples.en: I hear that every restaurant is badly short of staff these days.

examples.ko: 그 공장은 인력난 때문에 문을 닫을 뻔했어요.
examples.en: That factory almost closed because of a labor shortage.

examples.ko: 농촌은 젊은 사람이 없어서 인력난을 겪어요.
examples.en: Rural areas suffer from labor shortages because there are no young people.
If the labor shortage continues, wages sometimes rise.

examples.ko: 병원이 인력난을 해결하려고 직원을 더 뽑아요.
examples.en: The hospital is hiring more staff to solve its manpower shortage.
A sudden staff shortage came up, so everyone worked overtime.

explain: '-난'은 구하기 어렵다는 뜻을 더하는 말로 '구인난', '취업난'과 같은 방식이에요. 일할 사람이 모자란 회사나 업계 입장에서 쓰고, 일상에서는 '일손이 부족하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: The suffix '-난' adds the sense of difficulty or shortage, as in '구인난' and '취업난'. It is used from the viewpoint of a company or industry short of workers, and in daily talk people also say '일손이 부족하다'.

examples.en: My older brother studies political science at university.
Political science class has a lot of debate, so it's fun.
That person is a professor who teaches political science.

examples.ko: 저는 정치학과 경제학을 같이 배우고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to learn political science and economics together.

examples.ko: 정치학 책을 읽으면 뉴스가 더 잘 이해돼요.
examples.en: If you read political science books, the news is easier to understand.
I majored in international politics in graduate school.

explain: '정치'는 실제로 나라를 움직이는 일이고, '정치학'은 그것을 공부하는 학문이에요. 학과 이름은 '정치외교학과'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요. '경제학', '사회학'처럼 '-학'이 붙는 학문 이름과 같은 방식이에요.
explain_en: 정치 is the actual running of a country, and 정치학 is the field that studies it. Department names often read 정치외교학과. It follows the same -학 pattern as 경제학 and 사회학.

examples.en: The student council is preparing the festival this week.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 총학생회 회장을 뽑는 날이에요.
examples.en: Today is the day we choose the president of our school's student council.
The student council handed out snacks to the students.

examples.ko: 형은 대학교 때 총학생회 활동을 했어요.
examples.en: My older brother was active in the student council in college.
The student council held a meeting about the tuition issue.
If you have questions, ask at the student council office.

explain: 총학생회는 대학교 전체 학생을 대표하는 모임이에요. 한 학과나 한 반을 대표하는 '학생회'보다 범위가 커서 앞에 '총'이 붙어요. 대학생들은 줄여서 '총학'이라고 많이 불러요.
explain_en: 총학생회 represents all the students of a university. It is bigger than a 학생회, which covers one department or class, so it gets the prefix 총. University students often shorten it to 총학.
